P41.answer: The word starting with ה is at the left end of the line. Its ה is the letter I graded ח (probable) at Stage 1 pos 7 (A x~500-613; B x~445-507; C x~365-420). It is followed leftward by the box I read at Stage 1 as a single ט (pos 8) and by the small hook (pos 9). REVISION after re-inspection: in all three images the left leg of pos 7 stops short of the roof, so I now read ה (probable), not ח. The pos 8 box splits into two letters: an open box (letter 2) and a separate tall upright on its left (letter 3), because there is a gap between the base and that upright in B and C. My Stage 1 reading of ט assumed that upright was the tet's left arm.
P41.evidence: A: left leg starts ~20 px below the roof with a bright ridge between. B: left leg starts ~14 px below the roof. C: ~10 px gap. Right leg joined to the roof in all three.

P41.answer: Second letter: a box open on the left. Top: a short flat bar running left from the top of the right vertical (A x~460-500; B x~370-404; C x~282-316). At its left end a short tick rises above the bar, giving an L-shaped top in B and C and a thick tick in A. The right vertical rises slightly above the bar in B. Base: a straight, flat stroke at the foot (A x~400-500; B x~320-404; C x~248-316). In all three images it ends flush with the right vertical and does NOT project beyond it to the right. The lower-right corner is square, not rounded. So the absence of a projecting base points to כ, but the square corner and flat base are not the rounded kaf the question describes. My reading: כ possible, ב possible. I cannot decide between them on the base alone.
P41.evidence: A, B, C agree that there is no projection beyond the right vertical and that the corner is angular. The base is clearest in B (dark, straight). A shows a thick base meeting the vertical at a square corner. C shows the base ending at the vertical, with a small blob near its left end.

P41.answer: Third letter: ו (probable). It is a tall upright, the full height of the line (A x~390-410, y~205-363; B x~297; C x~222-232). At the top it has a head bending to the left (clearest in A, slight in B, rounded in C). Its foot stays separate from the base of letter 2: B gap ~15 px, C gap ~17 px, A only a few px. Its length rules out י.
P41.evidence: A: tall stroke with a left-hooking head. B: tall stroke, head bends slightly left, gap at the base. C: tall stroke with a rounded top, gap at the base.

P41.answer: Remaining letters: only one more mark is visible, a small hook or loop placed high in the line just left of letter 3 (B x~208-236, y~260-300; C x~168-200; A: a round bump at x~315-330 at the crack). Nothing reaches down to the baseline under it. This fits י (possible) better than a full-height letter. I see no ז: no full-height stem with a two-sided head. Last visible letter: that hook (י possible, ר/ד possible, or damage). The word does run to the edge. The hook sits directly against a crack and strip edge (B crack x~192-204; C dark hole and bright strip x~116-164; A crack x~310-330), and nothing legible on this line lies beyond it. Further letters, including a ז, could be lost there. Reading as seen: ה + כ/ב + ו + י? + [edge].
P41.evidence: B shows the hook most clearly as a small rounded head with a short stem. C shows a similar loop beside the dark hole. In A it coincides with a bump at the crack, so it might be corrosion.

P56.answer: I could not identify a ככ-like pair at the (left) end of the marked line. The left half (A x~300-700) is destroyed by a blister, a horizontal crack and the strip joint at x~600-690. B is unreadable there (dark hole and cracks). At Stage 1 I read the only shape near the left end as א (possible): A x~185-290, a thick down-right diagonal plus a thinner down-left diagonal that converge into a V. That V could equally be a non-unit numeral sign. No box-shaped letters (כ-like) are visible at the left end.
P56.evidence: A colour and high-pass crops of x~90-720. B high-pass crop of x~40-640 shows only cracks and the hole.

P56.answer: Possibly yes: the V- or angle-shaped mark at A x~185-290 (a thick '\' at 184-221 and a faint '/' at 261-290 converging toward the lower middle). It is not a vertical unit stroke. Whether it is a numeral sign or a letter (א/ע) cannot be decided.
P56.evidence: A only. B is unreadable here. It is crossed by a horizontal crack at y~215.

P56.answer: Possible vertical strokes, with low confidence: two thin, fairly straight verticals at A x~307-316 and ~330-338 (y~130-250), to the right of the V mark; and two very faint verticals at A x~102-107 and ~125-130 (y~200-290), at the strip edge to its left. Total: 2 possible plus 2 illegible. If they are strokes they would form two groups separated by the V mark (2 | V | 2), but I cannot exclude cracks, especially for the pair at 307-338, which looks thin and crack-like. Count: cannot tell.
P56.evidence: A column-darkness profile across y~170-280 shows dips at x~102-108, 123-126, 309-312, 330-336 and others at 213-219 and 240-243 (the V strokes). Visual inspection confirms only the two at 309-338 as clear lines. B: nothing visible.

P56.answer: Yes. (1) A large blister or flake at A x~340-500 (B: dark hole at a similar place) could hide several strokes. (2) A horizontal crack runs along the line from x~100 to 600. (3) The strip joint or cracks at x~600-690 could hide strokes. (4) The left strip edge at x~90 cuts off anything further left. (5) Surface erosion at x~140-180 and 240-300.
P56.evidence: A colour crop; B shows the hole and the horizontal crack.

P63.answer: Candidate ככ-like pair: the two box letters open on the left, Stage 1 pos 3 (A x~1005-1213: long curved roof, right vertical x~1180, base x~1072-1197) and the box at Stage 1 pos 5 (A x~800-907: short top bar running left from the right vertical x~899, base x~803-903). Between them is the low diagonal stroke of pos 4 (x~924-1016). REVISION: at Stage 1 I read pos 5 as ט, taking the upright at x~774 as its left arm. On re-inspection that upright has its own curled or hooked top and may be a separate sign, so the box alone reads כ-like (possible). B and D do not resolve this; the B right strip is washed out.
P63.evidence: A colour and high-pass crops. In A high-pass the x~724-787 stroke appears as a hook: a vertical with its top curling to the left.

P63.answer: Signs after the pair, in reading order (right to left), as seen in A, with B noted where it differs. (1) A hooked stroke at A x~724-787: an upright at ~775 whose top curls left and slightly down. Hook-like, possible; it may instead be the left arm of a ט. (2) A very tall upright at A x~640-665 (y~90-320) with a base running right to ~770. Possible sign, but B has a crack at x~600-660 here, so it may be a crack. In B this place shows a partial rounded arch (B x~555-615) cut by the crack. (3) A rounded arch or curled sign: A x~522-576 (two legs under an inverted-V or arch); B x~440-540, an arch with a long right leg and an inner diagonal curling in. Probable as a curled sign. (4) A second rounded arch: A x~388-480 (arch roof, thick right leg, dark inner curled stroke); B x~285-430 (arch whose right end curls inward). Probable. (3) and (4) look alike and sit side by side, so the hook sign is possibly doubled. B suggests a third similar arch at (2). Count of large hook or curled signs: 2 probable, 3 possible. (5) Vertical unit strokes left of the arches: A shows verticals at x~373 (short), ~338 (thick), ~295 and ~258, about evenly spaced (37-43 px), plus a doubtful one at ~220. B shows two verticals (B x~205, ~245) and a diagonal (B x~147-185). Unit strokes: 4 possible in A (2 in B). They look like one group; grouping cannot be told reliably.
P63.evidence: A high-pass crops of x~100-820. B high-pass crop of x~60-640, where the arches are clearest. D shows three rounded bumps on the left strip, consistent with arches.

P63.answer: Yes. The B crack at x~600-660 falls where sign (2) is and could hide or fake a stroke. A has a vertical crack at x~1012-1022 between the pair letters. The A surface left of x~230 is eroded and faint, so further unit strokes could be lost before the strip edge at x~100. The B right strip is washed out by wrinkles, so B cannot check the pair.

P92.answer: Candidate כ-פ: the two box letters with a curl at the top right that I read at Stage 1 as ט ט (pos 4: A x~735-848; pos 5: A x~590-702; B x~613-748 and ~470-590). In both, the top bar runs left from the right vertical and curls down inside the box at its left end, which is the פ-type mouth. Each also has an upright on its left. In B the left upright of the pos 5 box is joined to the roof of the next letter (B x~367-483), so it may belong to that letter rather than to the box. Read that way, the box would be פ-like, not ט. The pos 4 box has a closed small loop at the top right (A) or a dark knob (B), and its left upright has a left-pointing head. That makes ט, or ו + כ/פ, possible. I cannot confirm a כ followed by a פ. I report the stretch to the left of the pos 5 box as 'the word after it'. No word space is clearly visible anywhere.
P92.evidence: A tight crops at 4x. In B high-pass the roof from x~367 to 483 meets the upright at ~474-480.

P92.answer: Letters after the pos 5 box, right to left: (1) A letter with a roof (A x~540-600, faint curved roof at y~150; B x~367-483, clearer roof). Its right leg is the upright at A ~593 / B ~476. A long left leg slants down-left and runs below the baseline (A x~495 to 453, y~168-303; B x~355 to 317). A short inner upright sits at A x~515-525 (B ~386). Read ק (possible), or ה/ת. At Stage 1 I split this into pos 6 (ו) and pos 7 (?). (2) A x~360-438: an upright at ~413-427 whose foot runs down-left to ~360,270, with a small bowl or loop at x~313-382, y~155-233 (A high-pass). Illegible: נ, ע or ב possible. (3) A x~300-365: an upright at ~320 with a diagonal joining its top from the upper right. ע/צ possible. (4) A x~190-295: a roofed letter whose strokes run up into the line above (roof at y~75), with legs at ~195-205, ~265 and ~295. ח/ה/ת possible. Just left of x~190 the strip edge cuts the line.
P92.evidence: A high-pass crop of x~140-620 and B high-pass crop of x~80-640. In B the left part of the line is cut by bright wrinkles or the strip edge at x~<180.

P92.answer: Cannot tell. No closed box (ם) is visible at any likely word end. The long descender at A x~453-495 together with the short upright at ~515-525 could be read as י + ן (an -ין ending) if a word ended there. In B, however, both strokes look like parts of one roofed letter (ק/ה). The last letter before the strip edge (A x~190-295) is roofed (ח/ה/ת-like), not a clear ר. I can neither confirm nor exclude ין, ים or ר.
P92.evidence: A and B disagree on how to segment the strokes at A x~450-600.

P92.answer: Cannot tell. Between 4 letters (counting the ק/ה-like letter as one) and 6 (counting the inner upright and the long descender separately) are visible before the strip edge. The word boundary is not visible, and letters may be lost at the edge.
No numeral signs seen. There are no groups of short vertical unit strokes and no hook or curled numeral signs on this line. Everything visible has letter-like forms.
P92.evidence: A and B across the full line.
